title: Laptop Thermal Throttling at Idle
symptom: Laptop gets very hot on the bottom and fan is loud while idle, shutting down abruptly after 20 minutes of light use.

expected_output.symptom_summary: Laptop exhibits extreme heat dissipation failure and high fan RPM during low-load idle, causing automatic thermal shutdowns.

evidence.text: Laptop gets very hot on the bottom

possible_causes.cause: Heatsink fins clogged with compacted dust or lint, preventing thermal dissipation.
possible_causes.verification: Inspect heatsink exhaust vents with illumination to verify dust blanket.

possible_causes.cause: Degraded thermal compound on CPU/GPU die causing high thermal barrier.
possible_causes.verification: Log thermal sensors; observe core temperatures jumping to 95°C+ instantly under mild loads.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Ensure laptop is operated on a hard, flat surface with cleared intake vents.
troubleshooting_steps.rationale: Rules out simple airflow smothering from soft bedding or cloth surfaces.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Blow short bursts of compressed air into the exhaust vents while powered down.
troubleshooting_steps.rationale: Dislodges superficial dust clumps without opening the chassis.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check OS Task Manager for background processes consuming CPU cycles.
troubleshooting_steps.rationale: Eliminates rogue malware or crypto-miner software spikes.
